{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}'''Blackcomb Pipeline''' is a gas pipeline under construction in the United States.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/blackcomb-pipeline-reaches-final-investment-decision-to-transport-growing-natural-gas-production-from-the-permian-basin-to-the-gulf-coast-region-302211609.html|title=Blackcomb Pipeline Reaches Final Investment Decision to Transport Growing Natural Gas Production from the Permian Basin to the Gulf Coast Region|website=www.prnewswire.com|access-date=2025-10-15}}</ref>	
==Location==
The pipeline is proposed to run from the Permian Basin to the Agua Dulce area in Texas, United States.<ref name=":0" />

==Background==
The project has a T-4 permit under the Texas RRC of T-10643.<ref name=":1" /> It was proposed to transport gas from the Permian to the Agua Dulce hub in south Texas.<ref name=":2" />

According to the developer's website, as of October 2025: "The Blackcomb Pipeline is an approximately 366-mile intrastate pipeline designed to transport up to 2.5 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas from the Permian Basin to a terminus near Agua Dulce, Texas, providing direct access to South Texas markets and consumers. An approximate 80-mile, 42-inch lateral line will also provide connectivity for gas processors in the Midland Basin."<ref name=":3" />

WhiteWater MPLX LP and Enbridge Inc together form the WPC Joint Venture, and these entities partnered with Targa Resources to finance the project. FID was reached in July 2024.<ref name=":0" /> Reuters confirmed this was the initiation of the construction phase.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/whitewater-partners-move-forward-with-blackcomb-pipeline-construction-2024-07-31/|title=WhiteWater, partners to move forward with Blackcomb pipeline construction|work=Reuters|access-date=2025-10-15|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Lateral ===
The developer's website mentions an approximately 80-mile lateral that connects the pipeline to producers in the Texas Midland Basin. No evidence for this separate route can be found through research online, and it is presumed to be part of the route encompassed in the main line.
